First, we rewrite the polynomial, interpreting any constants as multiples of the identity matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(X) & ={X}^{2}+2X+2 \\  & ={X}^{2}+2X+2I\end{aligned}
$$

So, we want to find $f(A)={A}^{2}+2A+2I.$

Let's calculate ${A}^{2}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{2} & =A\cdot A \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 & -5 \\ 0 & 9\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can evaluate $f(A):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(A) & ={A}^{2}+2A+2I \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 & -5 \\ 0 & 9\end{aligned}]+2[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}]+2[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 & -5 \\ 0 & 9\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}4 & -2 \\ 0 & 6\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4+4+2 & -5+(-2)+0 \\ 0+0+0 & 9+6+2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}10 & -7 \\ 0 & 17\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
